Title: Purity Not Proven
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' is marked [EnforcePure]/[Pure], but its body contains operations the analyzer cannot prove pure
Description: Methods marked with [EnforcePure] require analysis. This diagnostic indicates the analysis rules did not determine the method's purity status. Use `SharpProof.SymbolicCli explain --file <path> --line <number>` to inspect the symbolic proof evidence.

Title: Misplaced [EnforcePure] Attribute
MessageFormat: The [EnforcePure]/[Pure] attributes can only be applied to method-like declarations or getter-bearing properties and indexers
Description: [EnforcePure] and [Pure] configure purity analysis for a method-like declaration or alias the getter of a getter-bearing property or indexer.

Title: Missing [EnforcePure] Attribute
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' appears to be pure but is not marked with [EnforcePure]. Consider adding the attribute to enforce and document its purity.
Description: This method seems to only contain operations considered pure, but it lacks the [EnforcePure] attribute. Adding the attribute helps ensure its purity is maintained and communicates intent.

Title: Conflicting purity attributes
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' has conflicting purity attributes applied
Description: Apply one purity contract to a method. Combining enforcing, trusted-external, and explicit-impure attributes is contradictory or confusing.

Title: [AllowSynchronization] requires a purity attribute
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' is marked with [AllowSynchronization] but is not marked with [EnforcePure] or [Pure]
Description: [AllowSynchronization] only affects methods participating in purity analysis. Apply [EnforcePure] or [Pure] for it to have effect.

Title: Misplaced [AllowSynchronization] Attribute
MessageFormat: The [AllowSynchronization] attribute can only be applied to method declarations
Description: [AllowSynchronization] configures analyzer behavior for a method and should not be used on non-method declarations.

Title: Redundant [AllowSynchronization]
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' is marked with [AllowSynchronization] but contains no synchronization constructs
Description: Remove [AllowSynchronization] when the method does not use synchronization (e.g., lock).

Title: Purity Diagnostic Explanation
MessageFormat: Purity analysis for '{0}': {1}
Description: Provides structured explanation data for a purity diagnostic.

Title: Method May Throw Exceptions
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' can throw: {1}
Description: Reports exception types that can escape a method. Enable with sharpproof_report_exceptions = true or sharpproof_runtime_hazard_mode = summaries/all/all-and-unknowns. Use `SharpProof.SymbolicCli explain --file <path> --line <number>` to inspect the exception proof evidence.

Title: Operation May Throw Uncaught Exceptions
MessageFormat: Operation '{0}' may throw uncaught exceptions: {1}
Description: Reports uncaught exceptions and proven runtime hazards at specific operations. Enable with sharpproof_checked_exceptions = true or sharpproof_runtime_hazard_mode = sites/all/sites-and-unknowns/all-and-unknowns. Use `SharpProof.SymbolicCli explain --file <path> --line <number>` to inspect the runtime hazard evidence.

Title: BCL Purity Fallback Guess
MessageFormat: BCL purity fallback for '{0}': {1} ({2})
Description: Reports a non-authoritative purity guess for a metadata BCL member when no stronger analyzer, attribute, generated summary, or user configuration evidence was available. Enable with sharpproof_emit_explanations or sharpproof_report_bcl_fallback_guesses.

Title: Allocation In [ZeroAllocations] Method
MessageFormat: Method '{1}' is marked [ZeroAllocations], but operation '{0}' allocates
Description: Reports direct source-visible allocation sites inside methods annotated with [ZeroAllocations].

Title: Misplaced [ZeroAllocations] Attribute
MessageFormat: The [ZeroAllocations] attribute can only be applied to method-like declarations or getter-bearing properties and indexers
Description: [ZeroAllocations] configures allocation analysis for a method-like declaration or aliases the getter of a getter-bearing property or indexer.

Title: Disallowed Capability Use
MessageFormat: Method '{1}' is marked [AllowedCapabilities], but operation '{0}' requires capabilities: {2}
Description: Reports source-visible operations or proven transitive callees that exceed the method's declared allowed capability set.

Title: Capability Contract Not Proven
MessageFormat: Method '{1}' is marked [AllowedCapabilities], but operation '{0}' could not be capability-verified: {2}
Description: Reports operations whose capability set could not be conservatively proven under the current capability analysis. Use `SharpProof.SymbolicCli explain --file <path> --line <number>` to inspect the capability proof evidence.

Title: Misplaced [AllowedCapabilities] Attribute
MessageFormat: The [AllowedCapabilities] attribute can only be applied to method-like declarations or getter-bearing properties and indexers
Description: [AllowedCapabilities] configures capability analysis for a method-like declaration or aliases the getter of a getter-bearing property or indexer.

Title: Postcondition Not Proven
MessageFormat: Method '{1}' is marked [Ensures], but return site '{0}' does not prove postcondition '{2}'
Description: Reports return sites that contradict a declared [Ensures] postcondition. Use `SharpProof.SymbolicCli explain --file <path> --line <number>` to inspect the proof evidence for each return site.

Title: Postcondition Could Not Be Verified
MessageFormat: Method '{1}' is marked [Ensures], but postcondition '{0}' could not be verified: {2}
Description: Reports [Ensures] contracts that could not be parsed, lowered, or proven within the supported bounded proof surface. Use `SharpProof.SymbolicCli explain --file <path> --line <number>` to inspect the unprovable contract details.

Title: Misplaced [Ensures] Attribute
MessageFormat: The [Ensures] attribute can only be applied to method-like declarations or getter-bearing properties and indexers
Description: [Ensures] configures symbolic postcondition analysis for a method-like declaration or aliases the getter of a getter-bearing property or indexer.

Title: Declared Complexity Exceeded
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' is marked [ExpectedComplexity({1})], but inferred complexity '{2}' exceeds the declared bound
Description: Reports methods whose inferred bounded complexity is stronger than the declared [ExpectedComplexity] contract allows. Use `SharpProof.SymbolicCli explain --file <path> --line <number>` to inspect the complexity proof evidence.

Title: Declared Complexity Could Not Be Verified
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' is marked [ExpectedComplexity({1})], but the declared bound could not be verified conservatively: {2}
Description: Reports [ExpectedComplexity] contracts that could not be verified because the inferred complexity is unknown, unsupported, or incomparable with the declared bound. Use `SharpProof.SymbolicCli explain --file <path> --line <number>` to inspect the complexity analysis details.

Title: Misplaced [ExpectedComplexity] Attribute
MessageFormat: The [ExpectedComplexity] attribute can only be applied to method-like declarations or getter-bearing properties and indexers
Description: [ExpectedComplexity] configures complexity analysis for a method-like declaration or aliases the getter of a getter-bearing property or indexer.

Title: Invalid SharpProof Contract Argument
MessageFormat: SharpProof contract '{0}' has invalid argument '{1}': {2}
Description: Reports malformed SharpProof contract arguments, such as empty [Ensures] conditions, undefined [ExpectedComplexity] values, unknown [AllowedCapabilities] bits, and non-exception [AllowedExceptions] types.

Title: Invalid SharpProof Analyzer Configuration
MessageFormat: SharpProof analyzer option '{0}' has invalid value '{1}': {2}
Description: Reports invalid sharpproof_* analyzer configuration values that would otherwise fall back to defaults silently.

Title: Unrecognized SharpProof Attribute Identity
MessageFormat: Attribute '{0}' looks like a SharpProof contract, but type '{1}' is not in an accepted SharpProof attribute namespace
Description: Reports attributes whose simple name matches a SharpProof contract attribute but whose containing namespace is neither SharpProof.Attributes nor an opt-in source-stub namespace.

Title: Precondition Not Proven
MessageFormat: Call to '{0}' does not prove precondition '{1}'
Description: Reports calls whose current path facts contradict a declared [Requires] precondition. Use `SharpProof.SymbolicCli explain --file <path> --line <number>` to inspect the proof evidence.

Title: Precondition Could Not Be Verified
MessageFormat: Precondition '{1}' for '{0}' could not be verified: {2}
Description: Reports [Requires] contracts that could not be parsed, lowered, or proven within the supported bounded proof surface. Use `SharpProof.SymbolicCli explain --file <path> --line <number>` to inspect the unprovable contract details.

Title: Misplaced [Requires] Attribute
MessageFormat: The [Requires] attribute can only be applied to method-like declarations
Description: [Requires] configures symbolic call-site precondition analysis for a method-like declaration. On a property or indexer, place it on the explicit get accessor.

Title: Exception Contract Violated
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' is marked {1}, but operation '{2}' can throw disallowed exceptions: {3}
Description: Reports operations whose escaping exceptions violate [DoesNotThrow] or [AllowedExceptions] contracts. Use `SharpProof.SymbolicCli explain --file <path> --line <number>` to inspect the exception proof evidence.

Title: Misplaced Exception Contract Attribute
MessageFormat: The [DoesNotThrow] and [AllowedExceptions] attributes can only be applied to method-like declarations or getter-bearing properties and indexers
Description: [DoesNotThrow] and [AllowedExceptions] configure exception analysis for method-like declarations or alias the getter of a getter-bearing property or indexer.

Title: Invalid SharpProof Analyzer Additional File
MessageFormat: SharpProof analyzer input file '{0}' is invalid: {1}
Description: Reports malformed, empty, unsupported, or partially ignored SharpProof analyzer AdditionalFiles instead of silently dropping their data.

Title: Runtime Hazard Candidate Could Not Be Proven
MessageFormat: Runtime hazard candidate '{0}' at operation '{1}' could not be proven: {2}
Description: Reports bounded runtime-hazard candidates whose trigger could not be proven or rejected. Enable with sharpproof_runtime_hazard_mode = unknowns, sites-and-unknowns, or all-and-unknowns. The diagnostic is informational by default and carries stable proof, reason, trigger, and baseline metadata.

Title: Inferred [ZeroAllocations] Contract
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' has {1}; consider adding {2} ({3} confidence)
Description: Reports opt-in inferred contract candidates backed by bounded analyzer evidence. Enable with sharpproof_suggest_inferred_contracts and filter by family, visibility, and confidence.

Title: Inferred [AllowedCapabilities] Contract
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' has {1}; consider adding {2} ({3} confidence)
Description: Reports opt-in inferred contract candidates backed by bounded analyzer evidence. Enable with sharpproof_suggest_inferred_contracts and filter by family, visibility, and confidence.

Title: Inferred [ExpectedComplexity] Contract
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' has {1}; consider adding {2} ({3} confidence)
Description: Reports opt-in inferred contract candidates backed by bounded analyzer evidence. Enable with sharpproof_suggest_inferred_contracts and filter by family, visibility, and confidence.

Title: Inferred Exception Contract
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' has {1}; consider adding {2} ({3} confidence)
Description: Reports opt-in inferred contract candidates backed by bounded analyzer evidence. Enable with sharpproof_suggest_inferred_contracts and filter by family, visibility, and confidence.

Title: Inferred [Ensures] Contract
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' has {1}; consider adding {2} ({3} confidence)
Description: Reports opt-in inferred contract candidates backed by bounded analyzer evidence. Enable with sharpproof_suggest_inferred_contracts and filter by family, visibility, and confidence.

Title: Inferred [Requires] Contract
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' has {1}; consider adding {2} ({3} confidence)
Description: Reports opt-in inferred contract candidates backed by bounded analyzer evidence. Enable with sharpproof_suggest_inferred_contracts and filter by family, visibility, and confidence.

Title: Trusted Purity Boundary Review
MessageFormat: Purity trust source '{0}' for '{1}' was {2}{3}
Description: Reports structured, opt-in audit evidence for applied and overridden purity trust shortcuts.

Title: Nullable return contract violated
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' can return null despite contract '{1}'
Description: Reports a reachable normal return that violates the declared nullable return contract.

Title: Nullable parameter postcondition violated
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' can complete with parameter '{1}' null despite contract '{2}'
Description: Reports a reachable normal completion that violates a nullable parameter postcondition.

Title: Nullable member contract violated
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' can complete with member '{1}' null despite contract '{2}'
Description: Reports a reachable normal completion that violates a member-not-null contract.

Title: Null-forgiving operator is unsafe
MessageFormat: Null-forgiving operator can suppress a feasible null value for '{0}'
Description: Reports a null-forgiving operator reached by a proven null execution.

Title: Null-forgiving operator is unnecessary
MessageFormat: Null-forgiving operator is unnecessary because '{0}' is proven non-null
Description: Reports a null-forgiving operator whose operand is already proven non-null.

Title: Nullable contract can be declared
MessageFormat: Method '{0}' satisfies nullable contract '{1}'
Description: Suggests a nullable contract proved by every relevant completion path.

Title: Nullable verification was inconclusive
MessageFormat: Nullable contract '{1}' on '{0}' could not be verified: {2}
Description: Reports bounded nullable proofs that ended as unsupported or unknown.

Title: Awaiting a null-conditional expression
MessageFormat: Awaiting null-conditional expression '{0}' can dereference a null awaitable
Description: A null-conditional invocation produces a null awaitable when its receiver is null. Coalesce to a non-null awaitable or guard the receiver before awaiting.

Title: Task converted to text without awaiting
MessageFormat: Task expression '{0}' is converted to text instead of awaiting its result
Description: String concatenation and interpolation call ToString on Task objects; they do not use the asynchronous result.

Title: TaskCompletionSource may run continuations synchronously
MessageFormat: TaskCompletionSource construction '{0}' does not prove RunContinuationsAsynchronously
Description: TaskCompletionSource should normally include TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously to prevent completing threads from running arbitrary continuations inline.

Title: Async void method is not an event handler
MessageFormat: Async void method '{0}' is not an event handler; return Task so callers can observe completion and exceptions
Description: Async void prevents callers from awaiting completion and routes exceptions through the current synchronization context. It is reserved for event-handler-shaped methods.

Title: Async method blocks on asynchronous work
MessageFormat: Async method '{0}' synchronously blocks on '{1}'
Description: Calling Task.Result, Task.Wait, or GetAwaiter().GetResult() inside async code can deadlock or starve worker threads. Await the operation instead.

Title: Task-returning method returns null
MessageFormat: Task-returning method '{0}' returns null; callers that await it will throw
Description: A non-async method whose declared return type is Task or Task<T> must return a task object, not null.

Title: Task used as a disposable resource
MessageFormat: Task expression '{0}' is disposed by using instead of awaiting its result
Description: Using a Task disposes the task object; it does not await the asynchronous operation or manage the resource produced by that operation.

Title: Public async parameter validation is deferred
MessageFormat: Validation in async method '{0}' is captured by the returned task; use a synchronous wrapper when fail-fast argument validation is required
Description: Exceptions thrown from an async Task method, including validation before its first await, are stored in the returned task. A synchronous wrapper is required when callers must observe argument errors at invocation time.

Title: Collection mutated during enumeration
MessageFormat: Collection '{0}' is mutated by '{1}' while it is being enumerated
Description: Mutating the same ordinary mutable collection inside its foreach body invalidates the active enumerator and commonly throws InvalidOperationException.

Title: For-loop variable captured by an escaping closure
MessageFormat: For-loop variable '{0}' is captured by a closure that can observe a later iteration value
Description: For-loop iteration variables are shared across iterations. Copy the value into a local inside the loop before capturing it in a lambda that can escape the iteration.

Title: Struct exposes mutable instance state
MessageFormat: Struct '{0}' has mutable instance state; copies can be modified independently
Description: Mutable value types are frequently modified through accidental copies. Prefer readonly struct, record struct with immutable members, or a class when shared mutation is intended.

Title: Owned disposable field has no owner disposal contract
MessageFormat: Type '{0}' creates disposable field '{1}' but does not implement '{2}'
Description: A field initialized or assigned from a local allocation is owned by its containing type. The owner must expose the matching deterministic disposal lifecycle.

Title: HttpClient created repeatedly inside a loop
MessageFormat: HttpClient is created inside loop '{0}'; reuse a client or use IHttpClientFactory
Description: Repeated HttpClient construction creates avoidable connection pools and can exhaust sockets under sustained load.

Title: Shared state mutated by a parallel callback
MessageFormat: Shared state '{0}' is mutated in '{1}' without visible synchronization
Description: Captured locals and fields mutated by Task, Thread, timer, or Parallel callbacks require synchronization such as Interlocked or lock, or should be replaced with isolated state.

Title: Concurrent collection enumerated through LINQ
MessageFormat: LINQ operator '{0}' enumerates concurrent collection '{1}' without snapshot guarantees
Description: Concurrent collection members have documented concurrency behavior, but interface and LINQ extension methods do not necessarily provide an atomic snapshot.

Title: Value boxed inside a loop
MessageFormat: Value of type '{0}' is boxed inside loop '{1}'
Description: Repeated boxing allocates objects and adds GC pressure. Prefer generic APIs or strongly typed interfaces in repeated paths.

Title: Maybe-null query result is dereferenced
MessageFormat: Result of '{0}' can be null or empty-default and is dereferenced immediately
Description: Default-returning lookup and LINQ APIs require a guard, a non-null fallback, or a proof that a matching element exists before dereference.

Title: Queryable is materialized before further filtering
MessageFormat: '{0}' materializes IQueryable before subsequent '{1}' processing
Description: Compose supported filters and projections on IQueryable before materialization so the remote provider can execute them.

Title: Deferred query lambda mutates state
MessageFormat: Deferred LINQ operator '{0}' contains state mutation '{1}'
Description: Side effects in deferred LINQ lambdas run on every enumeration and can therefore execute zero, one, or multiple times unexpectedly.

Title: Queryable expression calls source-only method
MessageFormat: Queryable operator '{0}' calls source method '{1}' that the remote provider may not translate
Description: Remote IQueryable providers translate a bounded method set. Source-only helper calls in query predicates and selectors require provider-specific translation support.

Title: Serialized source type has a reference cycle
MessageFormat: Type '{0}' contains a serializable reference cycle and is serialized without explicit cycle handling
Description: System.Text.Json rejects reachable object cycles by default. Project cyclic entities to DTOs, ignore a link, or configure deliberate reference handling.

Title: Serializer ignores attribute from another JSON library
MessageFormat: Serializer '{0}' does not honor attribute '{1}' on member '{2}'
Description: Newtonsoft.Json and System.Text.Json define similarly named attributes that are not interchangeable.

Title: Required attribute cannot reject a non-nullable value type default
MessageFormat: [Required] on non-nullable value member '{0}' cannot distinguish omitted input from default({1})
Description: Use a nullable value type when model binding must distinguish missing input, then validate the resulting value range separately.

Title: Allocation length uses unchecked arithmetic
MessageFormat: Allocation length expression '{0}' can wrap before bounds validation
Description: Compute allocation sizes in a checked context so overflow is reported instead of becoming a wrapped negative or undersized length.

Title: Diagnostic suppression lacks justification
MessageFormat: Suppression '{0}' has no reviewable diagnostic scope or justification
Description: Broad pragma suppressions and SuppressMessage attributes without justification hide warning debt and should be narrowed or documented.

Title: Nullable analysis explicitly disabled
MessageFormat: Nullable analysis is disabled for this source region
Description: Explicit nullable-disable directives create blind spots in compile-time null-state analysis. Prefer scoped annotations and resolved warnings.

Title: Binary operation uses the same value on both sides
MessageFormat: Operation '{0}' uses '{1}' as both operands; verify that the second operand is correct
Description: Identical stable operands in built-in comparisons, subtraction, division, and remainder usually indicate a copied or mistyped operand. Floating-point and user-defined operators are excluded because they need not be reflexive.

Title: Container-owned service is disposed by its consumer
MessageFormat: Service resolved by '{0}' is disposed by consuming code; the dependency-injection container owns its lifetime
Description: Services resolved from IServiceProvider are disposed by their owning service provider or scope. Consumers should not wrap the resolved service in using or call Dispose directly.

Title: Deferred query is never consumed
MessageFormat: Deferred query produced by '{0}' is never enumerated or materialized
Description: LINQ query operators are deferred. Constructing a query and discarding it performs no work and does not execute its predicate or selector.
